title: Follow-up: evaluate prefix-cache interactions (reuse vs eviction) and propose policy adjustments
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
- After enabling KV compaction in canary, we saw improved p99 on the bursty-mix scenarios overall, but one model/pool showed a regression correlated with increased eviction churn and lower prefix reuse.
- Hypothesis: current eviction policy v1 + compaction triggers are not prefix-cache-aware, and we’re paying either (a) too much eviction of useful prefixes (lower hit-rate => more prefill tokens) or (b) keeping prefixes too “sticky” under pressure (allocator pressure => admission control / allocation failures => tail spikes).

Goal
Evaluate prefix-cache interactions with KV cache eviction/compaction and propose concrete policy adjustments (and, if low-risk, implement in a small PR) that improve tail latency stability without materially regressing average latency or prefix hit-rate.

Non-goals
- Re-architect prefix cache storage format.
- Major kernel changes. Any kernel-facing changes should be limited to metadata/pointer stability assumptions already supported by the compaction engine.

Questions to answer
1) Under allocation pressure, are we evicting prefixes that would have been reused within the reuse window?
2) Are we protecting prefixes too aggressively such that decode KV for active requests gets squeezed (increasing allocation failures / compaction thrash)?
3) Do we need a separate budget/arena for prefix-cache blocks vs active decode blocks?
4) How should scheduler ‘cache pressure’ signals (ENG-2846) influence prefix retention and reuse decisions?

What to measure (must be broken down by region/pool/model_family/tenant_tier)
- Prefix cache
  - prefix_cache_hit_rate (requests w/ non-zero reuse)
  - prefix_cache_saved_prefill_tokens (tokens)
  - prefix_cache_entry_evictions (count)
  - prefix_cache_entry_age_at_eviction (p50/p95)
- KV allocator/compaction
  - kv_fragmentation_ratio (as defined in ENG-2842)
  - kv_allocation_failures (count)
  - kv_evictions_total (count)
  - kv_evictions_prefix vs kv_evictions_decode (if we can attribute)
  - compaction_bytes_moved, compaction_time_ms, compaction_budget_throttles
- End-to-end
  - request_latency_ms p50/p95/p99 split by routes: chat vs completions, streaming vs non-streaming
  - prefill_time_ms vs decode_time_ms attribution (where available)

Proposed investigation plan
1) Pull canary slices where regression was observed
   - Use KV cache health dashboard + tracing samples to isolate the exact pool/model and time window.
   - Confirm whether regression is driven by (a) increased prefill (lower prefix reuse) or (b) allocator pressure (alloc failures/compaction thrash) or both.

2) Compare three workload “shapes”
   - A) High prefix reuse (agentic loops / templates)
   - B) Mixed reuse + bursts (customer traces from SUP tickets)
   - C) Low reuse long-context (worst-case memory pressure)
   For each: quantify marginal value of keeping prefixes in cache vs freeing blocks for new decodes.

3) Evaluate candidate policy knobs (paper design + quick simulation)
   - Make eviction cost-aware:
     - Score(prefix) = expected_saved_tokens * reuse_probability - memory_pressure_penalty
     - reuse_probability approximated via recent reuse count + last_used_ts decay.
   - Separate quotas:
     - Reserve X% of KV cache blocks for active decode; prefix cache can use remaining but yields first under pressure.
     - Alternatively: prefix cache can exceed quota only if fragmentation_ratio < threshold and allocation_failures == 0.
   - Pressure-triggered prefix shedding:
     - When scheduler reports cache_pressure=HIGH, aggressively age out prefixes beyond a small reuse window (e.g., >N seconds since last use) before evicting active sequences.
   - Tenant tier fairness:
     - Under pressure, evict prefixes from low-tier tenants first (but keep a minimum floor so we don’t starve PLG workloads completely).

4) Decide deliverable scope
   - Option 1 (preferred): propose policy adjustments + implement lightweight metadata/priority changes in eviction selector (no new storage).
   - Option 2: spec only (ADR addendum) if changes touch too many surfaces for runtime-1.18.

Acceptance criteria
- No regression (>1%) in median latency on perf suite.
- p99 improved or unchanged in bursty-mix benchmark; specifically, remove the known regression pattern in the canary pool (as measured by perf-canary scenario from ENG-2854).
- Prefix cache hit-rate does not drop materially in high-reuse workloads (target: <=2% relative drop) OR if it drops, show that end-to-end p99 improves and prefill token cost doesn’t increase beyond agreed threshold.
- Clear, documented policy contract between scheduler cache_pressure and prefix retention/eviction behavior.

Deliverables
- Short design note in Confluence (link in ticket when ready) summarizing findings + recommended policy changes and default thresholds.
- If feasible in-cycle: PR adjusting eviction scoring / quota behavior and unit tests + simulator coverage for pathological cases.
- Update runbook guidance: what to look for when prefix hit-rate drops during compaction rollout (signals + safe toggles).

Notes / links
- Related work: ENG-2845 (Eviction policy v1), ENG-2846 (Scheduler cache pressure), ENG-2847 (Compaction triggers/budgets), ENG-2850 (Dashboard), ENG-2854 (Perf-canary).
- Recent observation: canary showed one model/pool where eviction rate increased while prefix_saved_prefill_tokens dropped (needs confirmation via metrics breakdown).

Risks
- Overfitting policy to canary pool could regress other pools (mitigate with multi-scenario benchmark gate + staged rollout).
- Adding per-entry scoring in eviction fast path could increase overhead (mitigate: coarse buckets, O(1) updates, avoid per-token work).

Owner checklist
- [ ] Identify regression pool/model and create a reproducible benchmark config.
- [ ] Produce a one-page summary: root cause + proposed knobs.
- [ ] Align with Sofia Ivanova on scheduler integration expectations.
- [ ] Align with Omar El-Sayed on allocator constraints / what signals are cheap.
- [ ] Decide: ship change in runtime-1.18.x or defer to 1.19 with ADR addendum.
comments: 2025-03-03 (Talia Benson): Creating as a follow-up from canary review. We need a clearer story on prefix-cache behavior under pressure before we expand to 25% traffic.

2025-03-05 (Sean Gallagher): +1. From SRE side, we need explicit rollback signals for “prefix hit-rate collapse” vs “allocator pressure” so oncall knows which lever to pull (disable compaction vs tighten prefix limits).

2025-03-06 (Lena Fischer): Taking. Plan is to start with the canary regression window and quantify whether it’s primarily prefill inflation vs allocation failures. Will propose a simple quota + pressure-triggered shedding policy first before anything more complex.
2025-03-08 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler hook is ready to provide cache_pressure={LOW,MED,HIGH} with hysteresis. Please define what prefix-cache should do at HIGH so we can document the contract.

2025-03-11 (Omar El-Sayed): Allocator can attribute evictions by “owner” (prefix vs active) if we plumb an owner bit through the block map metadata. Low-risk but adds some tagging work—flagging in case it helps with measurement.
